rows.qualifier: Amendment A is signed and effective from 1 March 2026, and it controls over the stale system export (D5, D10).
Amendment A applies only to accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026, so accounts opened in 2024 stay at the 12-month Addendum period.
Amendment A's 18-month period was not yet effective on 2026-02-15 (effective 1 March 2026), so the 12-month Addendum period applied on that date.
Draft Amendment B is unsigned, marked not approved, and was not approved by the Board.
Backups are governed separately by the Backup Retention Schedule.
The public trust page shows 12 months for EU accounts, but Amendment A (18 months for 2026 accounts) is not yet reflected on the page.
Amendment A states an effective date of 1 March 2026, which precedes its signing on 5 May 2026, so the change took effect retroactively relative to signature.
The export's configuration table was last updated 2025-11-30 and is stale for 2026 accounts.
The export has not been updated to reflect Amendment A, and no configuration action had been taken as of the 2026-05-20 audit note.

summary.text: EU retention for accounts opened on or after 1 January 2026 is 18 months under Amendment A, signed 5 May 2026 with an effective date of 1 March 2026; accounts opened before 2026 remain at 12 months. The system-of-record export and public trust page both still show 12 months and are stale, and the DPO has instructed reliance on the signed amendment. Standard retention is 24 months, backups are 35 days and sit outside the Enterprise Data Retention Policy, and Draft Amendment B has no effect.
